- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price spikes (e.g., near 94.51 or 93.62) — model reacts too aggressively, peaking too high then correcting.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects downward after peaks, failing to capture gradual decline or stabilization.
- Late-period (last 5–10 days) forecasts are often too high, suggesting model overestimates near-term volatility or ignores long-term trend.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — underestimates downward momentum until 2–3 days later.
- Forecasts for 30-day horizon show persistent bias toward lower values, especially when history includes recent high prices — model fails to “warm up” to higher expectations.
- When true outcome is near or above 85, model tends to underestimate — especially if recent history includes 85–90 range.
- Model overreacts to minor price fluctuations (e.g., 0.5–1.0 point changes) — overfits noise, leading to erratic short-term forecasts.
- Forecasts are often too smooth — fail to capture sudden reversals or sharp corrections in 3–5 day windows.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market events that occur within 5–7 days of forecast window — lagged response.
